previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, vasculitis, and POTS was admitted for acute abdominal pain triggered by stress and fatty food consumption. She experienced typical epigastric pain with nausea, but also new-onset diffuse crampy pain and lightheadedness, raising concern for orthostatic changes. She had a low-grade fever and a rash on her arm, though evaluation did not confirm active vasculitis. She was managed supportively with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. Her condition improved gradually, with successful transition to oral intake and pain control. Methotrexate was administered during admission, and plans were made to increase the dose post-discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating oral intake, with pain controlled and instructions to follow up with her providers.
